nutshell: Orlando's folk scene is small and spread out, and three forces shape it: Puerto Rico, theme parks and Florida's cattle-country past. The trad core is one owner-run pub, Claddagh Cottage. Its fiddler and banjo-player owners have hosted the Every-Other-Wednesday Irish session for 25 years and made the pub the Southeast's uilleann-pipe hub. Around it run a monthly circuit of Sunday-afternoon Irish sessions, a Friday bluegrass jam held in an Ocoee parking lot since about 1990, an invisible old-time jam in members' homes, a young, gender-neutral contra rebuilt in 2022, and a shape-note singing revived in 2024. Listening happens at Timucua's house-concert hall and in Central Florida Folk's library concerts, and no FM station airs a folk show. The heritage layer is bigger: bomba taught by Rafael Cepeda's great-granddaughter in Kissimmee, Venezuelan gaita, Haitian twoubadou, Eatonville's Hurston legacy, horseback quadrille at the Silver Spurs Rodeo, and Epcot heritage musicians since 1982.

venues.name: Fiddler's Green Irish Pub & Eatery
venues.notes: 'Serving our community since 1996'; live entertainment 7 days a week; Thursday open mic. Any trad sessions belong to the trad thread.

venues.name: Claddagh Cottage Irish Pub
venues.notes: Bought by musicians Scott Vocca and Vicki Gish, who met playing there. On moving it down the road (by 2018) they custom-built a stage for Irish and folk musicians. Session details are for the trad thread.

venues.name: Trout Lake Nature Center
venues.notes: Venue of 'Lake Eustis Folk' potluck concerts with a jam afterward.

venues.name: Fodor's Grove
venues.notes: Backup venue for CFF concerts (used e.g. Sep 2017, Jan 2019, May and Dec 2021 per flier archive). Appears to be a private property; treat as a house-concert venue (low confidence).

venues.name: Corzic Music
venues.place: Eatonville / Orlando, 997 W Kennedy Blvd A1
venues.notes: Music store with acoustic instruments and a Plek repair center; hosts the OASIS dulcimer club monthly.

venues.name: The Abbey
venues.notes: Listed as a 'listening room' by Undiscovered Music, but no folk bookings were verified in 2026 (site blocks automated fetch; current listings found were tribute/candlelight shows). Low folk relevance.

venues.name: Stardust Video & Coffee
venues.notes: Indie/punk coffeehouse-bar; a folk directory lists a 2nd-Tuesday open mic (7-10 pm). The late-Oct 2026 calendar shows rock and themed nights, so folk relevance is low.

venues.name: Broken Strings Taproom (formerly Broken Strings Brewery)
venues.notes: Hosts the 2nd-Sunday old-time jam. Operated by Three Odd Guys Brewing.

venues.name: The Castle Irish Pub & Restaurant
venues.notes: Hosts the 4th-Sunday Irish session (FSFA). Shows Gaelic games on TV.

venues.name: An Tobar Irish Pub
venues.place: Sheraton Orlando North, 600 Lake Destiny Dr, Maitland
venues.notes: Hosts the 1st-Sunday Irish session (FSFA).

venues.name: Stephie's Pub & Irish Eatery
venues.notes: Hosts the 3rd-Sunday Irish session (FSFA).

venues.name: Winter Park Ballroom Dance Co.
venues.notes: Home of Orlando Contra Dance. It has a suspended hardwood floor, and dancers go to Jeremiah's Italian Ice next door afterwards.

venues.name: Casselberry Recreation Center / Secret Lake Park Dance Hall
venues.notes: Home of the Casselberry Hoedowners square dance club. It was also home of the Orlando Last Saturday Contra Dance from at least 2008 to about 2020.

venues.name: Cassia Community Club
venues.notes: A 1940s schoolhouse run as a nonprofit community club, 'known throughout Central Florida for our Country/Bluegrass jams' under oak trees.

venues.name: Ocoee parking lot (10870 W Colonial Dr)
venues.notes: A former Piggly Wiggly lot behind a Pizza Hut. Bring a lawn chair.

venues.name: Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church
venues.notes: Hosts the monthly shape-note singing and the January 2027 all-day singing.

venues.name: St. Paul's Presbyterian Church
venues.notes: Hosted the 1st (2024) and 2nd (2025) Central Florida All-Day Sacred Harp Singings.

venues.name: La Hacienda Recreation Center
venues.place: 1200 Avenida Central, Lady Lake (The Villages, Lake Co.)
venues.notes: Hosts the Orange Blossom Squares Sunday dances.

venues.name: Roth Family JCC at Shalom Orlando
venues.notes: Hosts Israeli folk dancing on Monday nights.

venues.name: First Baptist Church of Mount Dora
venues.notes: Hosts the Central Florida Dulcimer Festival, with RV parking contracted through the church.

venues.name: Raglan Road Irish Pub
venues.notes: Opened 21 Oct 2005 (WDWMAGIC). Has professional Irish bands and dancers nightly. It is a performance and tourist venue, not a participatory session.

organizations.name: Escuela de Bomba y Plena Tata Cepeda (performing group: Kalinda)
organizations.notes: Kissimmee. Founded by Barbara Liz Cepeda (Ortiz), great-granddaughter of Don Rafael Cepeda; first school in Central Florida dedicated to bomba and plena (https://www.wusf.org/arts-culture/2021-01-14/one-dance-teacher-goes-virtual-and-brings-bomba-and-plena-to-a-new-stage). 2024-25 state grant application projected 3,837 people engaged and 11 events (https://files.floridados.gov/media/707652/traditional-arts-98500.pdf).

organizations.name: Plenamar Latino
organizations.notes: Founded in Puerto Rico in 2005, now Orlando-based (Jimmy Castro); behind the viral Kissimmee Walmart parrandas of 2016-17; on the SanSe Orlando 2026 bill.

organizations.name: Proyecto Plena (Pleneros en Orlando)
organizations.notes: LLC registered Jan 30 2024 in East Orlando (https://www.flcompanyregistry.com/companies/proyecto-plena-llc/); gigs at parties and events (FL/PR).

organizations.name: Las Damas del Mundillo Orlando
organizations.notes: 'More than a dozen women' meet weekly; founded by Julia Belen Alverio; presented at the Florida Folk Festival Folklife Stage three times.

organizations.name: Florida Puerto Rican Parade, Inc.
organizations.notes: 19,450 Facebook followers; also scholarships and a gala.

organizations.name: Desfile Puertorriqueno de Osceola
organizations.notes: Kissimmee.

organizations.name: New World Music School of Orlando
organizations.kind: music school (Puerto Rican cuatro lessons and workshops)
organizations.notes: 6582 University Blvd, Winter Park; cuatro workshops for all levels led by string teacher Tito Garcia ($25).

organizations.name: The Latin Music Institute
organizations.notes: Winter Park; teaches Puerto Rican cuatro, Venezuelan cuatro and Cuban tres; claims to be the only Orlando school teaching all three in one place.

organizations.name: Atardecer Llanero Internacional (Los Centauros del Llano)
organizations.kind: Venezuelan musica llanera ensemble and promoter
organizations.notes: Orlando-based harp, cuatro and maracas conjunto; promoted 'Atardecer Llanero con Ignacio Rondon' at Oricono Ranch, Clermont (Nov 24 2024) (https://www.tickeri.com/events/zcnspfoy3kyl/atardecer-llanero-con-ignacio-rondon).

organizations.name: Sabor a Gaitas
organizations.notes: Friday residency at Nando Grill, Oct-Jan.

organizations.name: Carnaval en Orlando
organizations.notes: Crowns carnival royalty in Orlando, teaches cumbia and other carnival dances, sends a delegation to Barranquilla's parades (2027 calendar posted).

organizations.name: Colombian Multicultural Integration / Encanto Caribe Musical
organizations.notes: President Javier Molinares; Saturday classes at First Baptist Orlando.

organizations.name: Mexico Lindo Orlando (Mexico Lindo Folkloric Ballet)
organizations.notes: Founder Gizela Maldonado (ex-UNAM folklorico ballet); ages 8 and up; 10th anniversary 2025 (https://thelatidobeat.com/2025/10/16/latinos-en-orlando-baile-y-el-folclore/).

organizations.name: Farmworker Association of Florida
organizations.notes: 1264 Apopka Blvd, Apopka; Dia de los Muertos, community dinners with mariachi and folklorico; Lilly Carrasquillo has worked with FWAF since 1987.

organizations.name: Yo Amo la Danza
organizations.notes: Formed in St. Isaac Jogues parish about 7 years before Oct 2025; director Jose Alvarez; performs most weekends; dances of Ecuador's four regions, including the masked aya uma.

organizations.name: Raymi Dance School
organizations.notes: Free weekly marinera class.

organizations.name: Savalou Twoubadou
organizations.notes: Orlando-based; 2,160 Facebook followers.

organizations.name: Greater Haitian American Chamber of Commerce (Orlando)
organizations.notes: Hosts the Haitian Heritage Celebration (May).

organizations.name: Capoeira Orlando
organizations.notes: East Orlando; Contramestre Folclore; weekly Friday music and roda; annual batizado.

organizations.name: Capoeira Angola Palmares Orlando
organizations.notes: Led by Professor Peixe in the lineage of Mestre No (Salvador, Bahia).

organizations.name: CBP Martial Arts Academy (Capoeira Brazil Pelo)
organizations.notes: 4,068 Facebook followers.

organizations.name: Sambatu Batucada (Orlando Samba Reggae)
organizations.notes: Advertises a weekly samba-reggae class (day not verified).

organizations.name: New Generation Branches Steel Orchestra
organizations.notes: 'Training kids and teens for 25 years in Orlando' as of 2012 (https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2012/06/19/steel-orchestra-is-all-about-the-kids-2/); leader StClair Balthazar; 501(c)(3) ruling 2016; rehearses in an industrial area off John Young Pkwy; on the road at Orlando Carnival 2024.

organizations.name: Orlando Carnival Downtown / Caribbean American Passport
organizations.notes: The Original Orlando Carnival Association (https://www.facebook.com/groups/807350216079798/) says it is the oldest carnival association in Central Florida.

organizations.name: Junkanoo Near You
organizations.notes: DeVaughan Woodside (Lake Mary) with Orlando apprentices; corporation registered about 2008 and dissolved 2010 (https://www.flcompanyregistry.com/companies/junkanoo-near-you-incorporated/), but the group name was still used at the Florida Folk Festival and Orlando Carnival (year of that post not verified).

organizations.name: Hindu Society of Central Florida
organizations.notes: Festivals including Navratri garba nights.

organizations.name: Gujarati Society of Central Florida
organizations.notes: Garba events; event archive back to 2015.

organizations.name: Nritya Sudha's Hindu Temple Rhythms
organizations.notes: Teacher Anjali Fluker has presented 14 arangetrams since 2016.

organizations.name: Vietnamese American Community of Central Florida
organizations.notes: Runs the Orlando Tet Festival and the Miss Vietnamese Community of Florida pageant; the community began with 1975 refugees and grew around Mills 50, 'Little Vietnam' (https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2025/04/30/orlandos-vietnamese-community-began-50-years-ago-after-saigon-fell/).

organizations.name: UCF Filipino Student Association Dance Troupe
organizations.notes: Tinikling and Sayaw sa Bangko; performs at Orlando festivals.

organizations.name: Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Church / Hellenic Dancers
organizations.kind: Greek Orthodox parish and dance troupes
organizations.notes: Greek Orthodox Society incorporated Dec 2 1929; over 650 active families; Hellenic Dancers (four troupes per https://www.happenin.city/happenins/orlando/orlando-greek-fest).

organizations.name: Scottish-American Society of Central Florida
organizations.notes: Runs the Central Florida Scottish Highland Games. Founding year from a secondary source (medium).

organizations.name: Rosie O'Grady's Highlanders Pipes and Drums
organizations.notes: Founded 1974 as Central Florida Pipes and Drums; renamed when Bob Snow's Church Street Station sponsored it from 1980 and had it play Saturday nights; calls itself Central Florida's oldest pipe band; practices Mondays in Apopka; teaches beginners.

organizations.name: Central Florida First Responders Pipes & Drums
organizations.notes: Free membership and free weekly lessons.

organizations.name: Watters School of Irish Dancing
organizations.notes: Founded by Myra Watters after moving to Orlando in 2001; 415 N Clarke Rd, Ocoee (plus Gainesville); three World Championship titles; teaches ceili team dances; hosts the Orlando Feis (https://www.shinesymposiums.com/myra-watters).

organizations.name: Central Florida Irish Dance
organizations.notes: Claims over 120 students competing.

organizations.name: Ho'ike Hawai'i
organizations.kind: Hawaiian and Polynesian dance competition nonprofit
organizations.notes: Orlando. Related halau: Halau Hula o Kaleooka'iwa, 5309 Moonglow Blvd, Orlando (https://alohaworld.com/directory/hula-dance/halauclasses/halau-hula-o-kaleookaiwa).

organizations.name: Association to Preserve the Eatonville Community (P.E.C.)
organizations.notes: Founded by N.Y. Nathiri to fight the widening of Kennedy Blvd; ZORA! Festival since 1990.

organizations.name: Mt. Pleasant Missionary Baptist Church
organizations.notes: Orlando; home church of hymn liner Deacon Troy Demps.

organizations.name: Silver Spurs Club
organizations.notes: Grew out of young Osceola ranchers riding Quadrille together after a May 1940 barbecue at Geech and Connie Partin's ranch; club formed after riding in Gov. Spessard Holland's 1941 inaugural parade; peewee, junior and adult Quadrille teams practice weekly.

organizations.name: Osceola History (Osceola County Historical Society)
organizations.notes: Pioneer Village at Shingle Creek (relocated settler buildings); has a Narcoossee chapter.

organizations.name: Central Florida Folk, Inc. (CFF)
organizations.kind: folk society (501(c)(3)); Folk Alliance International group member
organizations.notes: Incorporated May 2001, but its concert lineage runs to 'Live @ Leu' (July 1995). The public membership list (Oct 17, 2026) has 19 numbered entries, 13 unexpired; dues $25 individual / $40 family. Board: President Barry Brogan, VP Sigi Nagys, Treasurer/webmaster John M. Cunningham, Secretary Liz Nagys; media contact Sheila Anderson; flier creator and workshops Susan 'SusieCool' Trewick; sound Brett Cammack; song-circle host Brad Thompson (https://sites.google.com/site/susiecoolsongs/central-florida-folk/cffinfo). Website online since Mar 7, 2007.

organizations.name: Timucua Arts Foundation
organizations.notes: 25th anniversary 2025; City of Orlando proclaimed Sept 19 'Timucua Arts Foundation 25th Anniversary Day' (per search summary of https://orlandoshine.com/timucua-arts-foundation-celebrating-25-years-of-house-concerts-this-september/).

organizations.name: Black Cat Cafe Open Mic (First Unitarian Church of Orlando)
organizations.notes: Staff of about 7 volunteers: Chip D. (chair, emcee, tech), Mike H. (secretary) and others.

organizations.name: Orlando Area Stringed Instrument Society (OASIS)
organizations.notes: Founded and directed by Bing Futch; dulcimer-focused, all strings welcome; free membership with a mailed card.

organizations.name: Winter Park Ukulele Society
organizations.notes: 40-45 at monthly meetings; began as a small group meeting by Park Avenue in Central Park. Performing offshoot 'The Ukulele Drifters' plays nursing homes. Related Facebook communities: Orlando Ukulele Family, Joy Ukulele Club of Central Florida, Central Florida Ukulele Players.

organizations.name: NSAI Orlando Chapter
organizations.notes: Monthly critique/education meetings.

organizations.name: International Songwriters Guild - Orlando
organizations.notes: Monthly Zoom meetings; coordinated by Susan Trewick.

organizations.name: Friends of Florida Folk (FOFF) and 'OTownFOFF'
organizations.kind: statewide folk support org and Orlando spin-off (historic)
organizations.notes: In 2002 the Orlando Weekly pointed readers to the FOFF calendar (www.foff.org) and 'Orlando's independent spin-off group' (members.aol.com/OTownFOFF). Current status of the Orlando spin-off: not found.

organizations.name: Will McLean Foundation
organizations.notes: Has run the Will McLean Music Festival (since 1990/1991), song contest, youth program, scholarships and Sunday Sampler concerts in Dunnellon. Since 2022 it owns Florida Sand Music Ranch near Brooksville. Its contact phone is a 407 (Orlando) number. Outside MSA.

organizations.name: Orlando Contra Dance / Contra Knights
organizations.kind: contra dance series (CDSS-listed) and UCF student club
organizations.notes: Lead organizer and caller Joe Harrington. Funded in part by a United Arts of Central Florida grant (https://www.meetup.com/greater-orlando-contra-dance/). The on-campus UCF Contra Knights dances are dormant pending new student officers.

organizations.name: Central Florida Shape-Note Singing (OrlandoFaSoLa)
organizations.notes: Run by Rachel Speer (chair) and Dean Jens (secretary/arranger). About 30 named leaders at the 2024 all-day singing.

organizations.name: Central Florida Bluegrass Association (CFBA)
organizations.notes: Based in DeLand. President John Parrish, contact Pat Musselman. Runs the 3rd-Saturday jam and concert at Cassia and a CFBA Expo (18 Apr 2026). A search summary says it was filed as a Florida corporation in Jan 2024 (not independently verified).

organizations.name: Cassia Community Club
organizations.notes: Runs the 2nd- and 4th-Saturday jams.

organizations.name: Florida State Fiddlers Association (FSFA)
organizations.notes: Runs the official Florida State Fiddle Contest, the annual convention (45th held Oct 2026 at O'Leno State Park, which implies founding c.1981) and the statewide 'Regular Jams' list that is the best source for Orlando sessions. Membership is $20 individual / $30 family. Gives the Tom Staley Award.

organizations.name: South East Uilleann Pipers Club (SEUPC)
organizations.kind: regional piping club (AL, FL, GA, NC, SC, TN)
organizations.notes: Holds its annual South East Tionól at Claddagh Cottage (2024-2026, and 29-31 Jan 2027) and International Uilleann Piping Day there each November.

organizations.name: Central Florida Square & Round Dancers Association
organizations.notes: First business meeting was 15 Feb 1957 at the home of Mary and Hack Chilton. The first dance, the 'Charter Jamboree', was on 3 Mar 1957. Holds 5th-Saturday association dances and publishes 'Keepin Posted'.

organizations.name: Florida Federation of Square Dancers
organizations.notes: Has 'more than 60 clubs' in Florida. The 72nd state convention is 26-27 Feb 2027 in Deltona, and the 77th National Square Dance Convention will be in Daytona Beach on 28 Jun-1 Jul 2028.

organizations.name: Whirl & Twirl
organizations.notes: Oviedo.

organizations.name: Geneva Round Dance Club
organizations.notes: A Federation member in Geneva (Seminole Co.). Schedule not found.

organizations.name: Orange Blossom Squares
organizations.notes: The membership figure is from 2015. Membership is limited to residents of The Villages.

organizations.name: Orlando Israeli Folk Dancing
organizations.notes: Debbie Meitin.

organizations.name: RSCDS Orlando (Florida) Branch / Caledonian Scottish Country Dancers of Orlando
organizations.notes: The 'Orlando Branch' is the umbrella for ten Florida groups, from Pensacola to Broward. Its website (rscdsfloridabranch.com) no longer resolves, and no current Orlando class schedule could be verified (confidence low).

organizations.name: Florida Folk Dance Council (FFDC)
organizations.notes: Webmaster John Daly. Updates are supplied by Pat Henderson of Orlando.

festivals.name: Florida Puerto Rican Parade & Festival
festivals.notes: Organization established Sept 2016; parade through downtown Orlando since at least Apr 29 2017 (Orlando Sentinel photo caption). 2025: Apr 26, dedicated to Aguadilla; 2026: Apr 25, 10th anniversary of the organization, dedicated to Yabucoa.

festivals.name: Desfile Puertorriqueno de Osceola (Kissimmee Puerto Rican parade)
festivals.notes: First Puerto Rican day parade in Osceola County July 2011 near Osceola Heritage Park (https://us.placedigger.com/desfile-puertorriqueno-de-osceola2036068464.html); 10th year Sept 24 2023 in downtown Kissimmee with free music festival. 2024-26 dates not verified (medium).

festivals.name: La SanSe Takes Orlando (Fiestas de la Calle San Sebastian, diaspora edition)
festivals.notes: Jan 24 2026 at Central Florida Fairgrounds, 10,000+ expected; lineup included Plenamar Latino and Kalinda (Tata Cepeda school). An Orlando SanSe was already held Jan 13-14 2018 at the same fairgrounds (Orlando Sentinel 2017).

festivals.name: Viva Osceola!
festivals.notes: Osceola Chamber, Kissimmee Lakefront Park, free. '32 years' as of Oct 2025 and '29th' in Oct 2021 after a 2020 COVID gap, so it began c. 1992-93 (medium). 2025 local acts: Mexico Lindo Orlando folklorico, Luifer Cachazo.

festivals.name: Fiesta Calle Orange
festivals.notes: 27th year on Oct 26 2025 (so first in about 1999); 2026 on Oct 25. A secondary site claims 150,000+ visitors (unverified, low). Mostly commercial salsa/merengue/bachata stages rather than folk.

festivals.name: Three Kings Day (Dia de Reyes), Old Town Kissimmee
festivals.notes: Osceola Chamber, Jan 11 2026 (with camels); Alianza Center held a separate Three Kings evening at St. John's Episcopal, Kissimmee (https://mynews13.com/fl/orlando/news/2026/01/02/three-kings-day-preserves-latino-culture).

festivals.name: La Magia de los Tambores (Escuela de Bomba y Plena Tata Cepeda)
festivals.notes: Annual free multicultural drum showcase; 2025 edition (Dec 13, Orlando) doubled as a Parranda Navidena, 463 interested on Facebook.

festivals.name: ZORA! Festival (Zora Neale Hurston Festival of the Arts and Humanities)
festivals.month: late January-early February (season runs to October)
festivals.notes: Presented by the Association to Preserve the Eatonville Community (founded 1987) since 1990; about 10,000 at the first (https://grabthelapels.com/2022/03/22/zora-nathiri/), 20,000 over four days in 1992 (https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1992/02/02/event-gives-perspective-on-heritage/). 2026: 37th annual academic conference; outdoor festival Jan 30-Feb 1.

festivals.name: Orlando Carnival Downtown
festivals.notes: Began 1987 as a 'Carnival Party' organized by Johnson Gilbert with Gloria Chandler, Mark Modeste, Tina Stubbs and others (https://anydayguide.com/festival/873-orlando-downtown-carnival). 38th in 2025 (May 23-25, Tinker Field and Camping World Stadium). Self-described 'third-largest Caribbean Carnival in the US' (unverified). A rival Original Orlando Carnival Association also exists.

festivals.name: Pantastic Steelpan Jamboree
festivals.notes: Official kickoff of Orlando Carnival Downtown; 6-8 steel bands; Luminary Green Park; May 3 2025 and May 2 2026, free (https://www.orlandodancehall.com/wp-event/pantastic-steelpan-jamboree-2026/).

festivals.name: Central Florida Scottish Highland Games
festivals.notes: Central Winds Park, Winter Springs (Seminole Co.); 48th games Jan 17-18 2026 per City of Winter Springs (https://www.winterspringsfl.org/DocumentCenter/View/1148/2026--City-Events-and-Programs), implying first games c. 1978-79; Scottish-American Society of Central Florida founded 1976 (http://www.floridaleisure.com/central-florida-scottish-highland-games/, medium). Called 'the largest community event in Seminole County' (https://doorlandonorth.com/events/47th-central-florida-scottish-highland-games/). EUSPBA pipe-band competition listed. Sources disagree on edition numbering (46th/48th/49th).

festivals.name: Orlando Greek Fest
festivals.notes: Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Church, Maitland; free; Hellenic Dancers and live Greek music. Billed as the 48th annual in 2026 (Nov 6-8) (https://hoodline.com/2026/10/orlando-greek-fest-marks-48-years-in-maitland-with-free-admission-no-kids-zone/), which implies about 1979. Orlando Weekly (2024) instead says 'an annual tradition since 1962', the year the parish bought its first downtown property. Sources disagree.

festivals.name: Orlando Tet Festival (Hoi Tet Ve Nguon, Vietnamese American Community of Central Florida)
festivals.notes: Feb 7-8 2026 at Central Florida Fair, 4603 W Colonial Dr; lion dances, Miss Vietnamese Community of Florida pageant. WESH called an edition the '51st annual' (article year not verified). A second parish festival, the Central Florida TET Festival at St. Philip Phan Van Minh Catholic Church, ran the same weekend (https://www.gottagoorlando.com/post/the-2026-central-florida-tet-festival-returns-to-celebrate-vietnamese-new-year-in-orlando).

festivals.name: Thundering Spirit Family Pow Wow
festivals.notes: Renninger's Twin Markets, Mount Dora (Lake Co.). 23rd annual Mar 6-8 2026, so first in about 2004. 2025: Feb 28-Mar 2, $10 per day or $15 for three days, Aztec dancers, flute players, hoop dancing (https://www.clickorlando.com/news/local/2025/02/24/celebrate-native-american-culture-at-mount-doras-thundering-spirit-family-pow-wow/).

festivals.name: Spirit of the Buffalo Native American Festival and Pow Wow
festivals.notes: International Market World flea market, Auburndale (Polk Co.); 30th annual Jan 30-Feb 8 2026.

festivals.name: Silver Spurs Rodeo
festivals.notes: Silver Spurs Club (300+ members) staged its first rodeo, with war-bond admission and about 1,000 people, in March 1944 in the Partin pasture, Kissimmee; mid-winter rodeo since Feb 1951; 8,300-seat indoor Silver Spurs Arena since 2003. Includes Quadrille (square dance on horseback) and a Silver Spurs Rodeo Parade; Feb 2026 shows sold out.

festivals.name: Pioneer Day (Osceola History)
festivals.notes: Pioneer Village at Shingle Creek, Kissimmee; free; live music, pioneer crafts and Seminole life demonstrations. 33rd held Nov 8 2025 (https://www.aroundosceola.com/news-photo-gallery/step-back-time-pioneer-day-2025).

festivals.name: The Orlando Feis
festivals.notes: Annual CLRG double feis (Irish step-dance competition) hosted by the Watters School of Irish Dancing; May 24 2025 at Rosen Centre, back-to-back with the Alter Ego Feis (http://www.orlandofeis.com/Syllabus_Orlando_Feis_2025.pdf).

festivals.name: Ho'ike Hawai'i Hula Competition
festivals.notes: Two-day Hawaiian and Polynesian (Tahiti, Samoa, Aotearoa, Tonga) dance competition, 8001 International Dr. Freshest evidence: 2023 (https://www.hulafromtheheart.com/kumu-teacher). Its own site could not be loaded. Status medium-low.

festivals.name: Festival Independencia Dominicana
festivals.notes: Southport Community Park, Orlando; Feb 23 2025 and Feb 22 2026; organizer inspired by merengue tipico/perico ripiao (https://www.facebook.com/festivaldominicano/).

festivals.name: Colombian Independence Festival
festivals.notes: July 12 2025 at Festival Park, Orlando.

festivals.name: Festival Vallenato Orlando
festivals.notes: 3rd edition Oct 19 2025 at Simon Parrilla, 1187 Florida Mall Ave (tribute to Omar Geles), $20 presale, so the first was about 2023.

festivals.name: Bajada de la Chinita Orlando / Feria de la Chinita Orlando
festivals.notes: '8va Bajada de la Chinita en Orlando 2025' (so first in about 2018); Feria de la Chinita festival Nov 15 2025 with gaitas, tickets $50-120 (https://www.instagram.com/reel/DQUpva0CWbq/). Mirrors the Maracaibo feast of the Virgen de Chiquinquira.

festivals.name: Haitian Heritage Celebration (Greater Haitian American Chamber of Commerce)
festivals.notes: May 17 2025, Orlando. Haitian Flag Day (May 18) weekend otherwise means many kompa parties and balls.

festivals.name: Festa Junina (Resurrection Catholic Church)
festivals.notes: Billed as the largest festa junina in Central Florida, at Rancho Minha Terra, 18580 First St; the June 7 2025 date was postponed (https://www.tiosam.com/estados-unidos/florida/por-motivo-de-forca-maior-festa-junina-2025-em-orlando-e-adiada-nova-data-sera-anunciada/).

festivals.name: Dia de los Muertos at the Farmworker Association of Florida
festivals.notes: Apopka FWAF office, Nov 2 2025. FWAF's Oct 23 2026 community dinner featured mariachi and folklorico (https://theapopkavoice.com/stories/from-the-fields-to-the-family-table-farmworker-association-plans-apopka-community-dinner,189749).

festivals.name: Chaitra Navratri Garba (Gujarati Society of Central Florida)
festivals.notes: First spring Navratri garba in Central Florida, Apr 5 2025, Olympia High School: participatory Gujarati circle dance.

festivals.name: Great Florida Cattle Drive
festivals.notes: Jan 26-31 2026 from the DeLuca Preserve to Okeechobee. Saddle maker Mike Wilder (2008 Folk Heritage Award; makes Silver Spurs Rodeo prize saddles) was Cow Boss of the 2006 drive.

festivals.name: ZORA! Festival (Zora Neale Hurston Festival of the Arts and Humanities) / ZORA! Outdoor Festival of the Arts
festivals.month: Jan-Feb (outdoor festival; season runs Jan 7 to Oct)
festivals.notes: Presented by the Association to Preserve the Eatonville Community (P.E.C.). 2026 outdoor festival Jan 30-Feb 1 on E. Kennedy Blvd, Eatonville, $20-$100 (https://www.orlandoweekly.com/arts/zora-festivals-outdoor-festival-of-the-arts-is-the-place-to-be-in-eatonville-all-weekend/). Music is mostly R&B/soul/gospel headliners (2026: JUBU of Maze tribute, Brick), plus a line-dance day; it is a heritage and humanities festival rather than a folk-music festival. A secondary summary says the 1990 inaugural drew over 10,000 (https://www.britannica.com/question/What-annual-event-celebrates-Eatonvilles-cultural-heritage); not confirmed from a primary source, so attendance left null. last_evidence 2026-09.

festivals.name: Kissimmee Bluegrass Festival
festivals.month: early March (later reports suggest it moved to December)
festivals.notes: Kiwanis Club of Kissimmee fundraiser at the Silver Spurs Rodeo grounds (US 192). The first year (1977) lost $26,000, and by 1993 (16th annual) it had about 25 pro acts (Lewis Family, Chubby Wise) and more than 6,000 expected. Organizer Tom Rex called it the kickoff of the nine-month bluegrass season, and it was heavy on parking-lot picking. Chubby Wise played 'Orange Blossom Special' there in 1989 (https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1989/04/30/true-bluegrass-chubby-wise-can-make-a-fiddle-sing-sweeter-than-just/). It was still running in 2006 at Heritage Park, produced by Steve Dittman (https://www.baltimoresun.com/os-xpm-2006-03-01-owbluegrass01-story.html), and a Bluegrass Today post reviewed a 'Kissimmee Bluegrass Festival' in Dec 2016 (https://bluegrasstoday.com/review-of-kissimmee-bluegrass-festival/). No 2024-2026 evidence was found, so it is probably defunct (medium-low confidence).

festivals.name: Florida Folk Festival
festivals.notes: Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park, White Springs (Columbia/Hamilton Co.), about 170 mi north of Orlando. The 73rd was May 23-25, 2025 with 300+ performances; recent editions draw about 10,000-20,000 (secondary estimate: https://www.floridarambler.com/florida-festivals/florida-folk-festival/). It hosts the official Florida State Fiddle Contest. Central Florida Folk skips its May concert because members go to White Springs (https://cffolk.org/concerts/concerts.htm). Orlando-born Jeanie Fitchen first played its Old Marble Stage in 1966 at age 15.

festivals.name: Florida State Fiddle Contest (official)

Stat. 15.048 places it at the Stephen Foster center; https://florida.public.law/statutes/fla._stat._15.048). The secondary source above gives 1990; FSFA's own list says 1989. Divisions are Junior (12 and under), Youth (13-17), Twin, Open (formerly Contemporary) and Old Time (formerly Rustic), with two tunes in 4 minutes. The 2026 contest was held May 23. The 2020-21 contests appear to have been virtual ('2022 - Back to In-Person'). No fiddle contest inside the Orlando MSA was found.

It has 9 stages, 230+ performances, a workshop tent and two jam tents, an old-time barn dance with live callers, and the kids' 'Lil' Abner Fiddle Hunt'. Its spring twin is the Barberville Spring Frolic (first full weekend of April). FSFA lists a 1st-Saturday old-time jam and 4th-Saturday free old-time tutoring at the settlement (https://flafiddlers.wordpress.com/regular-jams/).

Morris), and 11 recordings from Caruja Ranch, Kenansville, Osceola County (July 1, 1940, Carita Doggett Corse and Robert Cornwall): a string band with 'violins', banjo and guitar plus Black singers James Brown and Rufus Bland. Zora Neale Hurston's June 18, 1939 Jacksonville session includes Eatonville-learned songs ('Mule on the Mount', learned from George Thomas of Eatonville). No items located in Orange or Lake County proper.

timeline.event: The Treaty of Moultrie Creek creates a Seminole reservation covering much of central Florida, including the future Orlando. The Second Seminole War and removal follow, and the 1842 Armed Occupation Act opens the area to white settlers. No metro-specific Seminole or Creek music recordings were found; documented Seminole song recordings (Densmore, Harry Jumper 1954) come from South Florida.

Orlando laid out as county seat (incorporated 1875). In 1875-1895, the citrus 'Golden Era', grove and cattle communities hold fiddle-and-square-dance gatherings, as later recalled by Richard Seaman (born 1904, Kissimmee Park).
Eatonville incorporated as an all-Black town (Orlando Sentinel 1990: 'founding 103 years ago'); Zora Neale Hurston later grows up here.

Eatonville is incorporated (Aug 15) as one of the first self-governing Black towns in the US. It is often billed as the oldest, but Brooklyn, Illinois (1873) is older. Goldsboro, another Black town by Sanford, incorporates in 1891 and is annexed by Sanford in 1911.
Fiddler and storyteller Richard Seaman born in an orange grove near Kissimmee Park; he learns from grove fiddlers who play for square dances.
Lutheran Slovaks from Cleveland found the Slavia colony near Oviedo (Seminole Co.).
Lake Eola bandshell (by Ida Annah Ryan and Isabel Roberts) dedicated Mar 23 with a program including a banjo solo by Charles Green
c. 1920s-1940s: Clayton Raulerson (b. 1906) drives cattle from Lake Okeechobee to the Orlando area as the cattle team's fiddler. 'All cattle teams had a fiddle player.'
Greek Orthodox Society 'Holy Trinity' incorporated in Orlando (Dec 2).

Zora Neale Hurston stages 'From Sun to Sun: A Day in a Railroad Camp' at Rollins College, Winter Park, with an all-Black Eatonville cast before a white-only audience, backed by professors Edwin Osgood Grover and Robert Wunsch.
June: Alan Lomax, Zora Neale Hurston and Mary Elizabeth Barnicle record in Eatonville (Gabriel Brown, Rochelle French) for the Library of Congress.

Hurston's Mules and Men is published, built on Eatonville and Polk County turpentine/lumber-camp collecting (Loughman). In June, Alan Lomax, Hurston and Mary Elizabeth Barnicle record 104 songs on 21 discs in Eatonville (Gabriel Brown, the Frenches, Rev. Haynes, children's singing games).
Vassar Clements, born 1928 in Kinard FL, grows up in Kissimmee and teaches himself fiddle at age 7 (c.1935). He joins Bill Monroe's Blue Grass Boys in late 1949.
Gamble Rogers born in Winter Park

WPA Florida Folklife: Aug 31-Sep 1, Alton C. Morris records the Slovak Lutheran youth chorus at St. Luke's, Slavia (30 items). On June 18, in Jacksonville, Hurston sings for Herbert Halpert and Stetson Kennedy the Eatonville-learned songs 'Mule on the Mount', 'Uncle Bud' and others.
May: young Osceola ranchers start riding Quadrille together after a barbecue on Geech and Connie Partin's ranch.

July 1: Carita Doggett Corse and Robert Cornwall record a cowhunter string band (Bob Hall, Walter Van Bass, Ned Hugh Bass, J. C. King on violins, banjo and guitar) and Black singers James Brown and Rufus Bland at Caruja Ranch, Kenansville, Osceola County. It is the metro's only WPA fiddle recording found.
Silver Spurs Club formed after riding in Gov. Spessard Holland's inaugural parade.
First Silver Spurs Rodeo (March, war-bond admission, about 1,000 people); first full-dress rodeo July 4.
First Silver Spurs Rodeo in Kissimmee (July 4, a war-bond benefit). It becomes Florida's official state rodeo in 1994, and Osceola schools still close for 'Rodeo Day'.
Kissimmee-raised Vassar Clements, 21, joins Bill Monroe's Blue Grass Boys, replacing Chubby Wise.
The Florida Folk Festival begins at White Springs (outside the MSA). It becomes Central Florida's annual folk pilgrimage.
Florida Folk Festival begins at White Springs; it becomes the annual pilgrimage that Orlando's folk calendar pauses for each May
The Central Florida Square Dancers Association is founded (15 Feb) and holds its 'Charter Jamboree' (3 Mar).

c. early 1960s: the Carrera Room folk coffeehouse opens in Hodgin's Restaurant, 534 S. Park Ave, Winter Park, later moving to 643 N. Orange Ave by Rollins. Gamble Rogers, Gram Parsons (with the Shilos), 17-year-old Bernie Leadon and Fred Neil play there. Opening year approximate.
Gamble Rogers and Alan Stowell persuade Rollins to sponsor Don Reno and the Tennessee Cut-ups at the Carrera Room.
David Ivey later recalled singing Sacred Harp in Central Florida in the 1960s (decade approximate).
Orlando teenager Jeanie Fitchen (15) first plays the Florida Folk Festival's Old Marble Stage.
The Carrera Room and Hodgin's Restaurant close.

Walt Disney World opens; Kauiihealani Brandt's hula troupe is recruited for the opening and stays, seeding Orlando's Polynesian dance community. Disney jobs also start the Puerto Rican migration to Central Florida.
Walt Disney World opens (Fort Wilderness Nov 1971), beginning the theme-park era that becomes the metro's biggest employer of 'heritage' performers.
Central Florida Pipes and Drums founded (renamed Rosie O'Grady's Highlanders under Church Street Station sponsorship in 1980).

Bob Snow opens Rosie O'Grady's Good Time Emporium (July 19), the seed of Church Street Station (one source says 1972). Disney's Hoop-Dee-Doo Musical Revue (country/vaudeville dinner show, Pioneer Hall) debuts that summer and goes full-time Sept 5.
Vietnamese refugees arrive after the fall of Saigon, later building 'Little Vietnam' in Mills 50.
Scottish-American Society of Central Florida founded; Highland Games follow (48th in 2026).
Apple Annie's Courtyard opens at Church Street Station (July) as its folk and bluegrass room, with house band Mother's Choice.

First Kissimmee Bluegrass Festival (Kiwanis) at the Silver Spurs grounds loses $26,000 but later becomes a fixture, with 6,000+ expected by 1993. First Barberville Fall Country Jamboree (Volusia) is also probably this year.
c. 1978-79: first Central Florida Scottish Highland Games (48th annual in Jan 2026).
First Central Florida Scottish Highland Games (inferred from the 48th in 2026).

song_listening.notes: CFF concert: $15 suggested, $10 members (Nov 2026). Timucua: '$30 or less', about half of events pay-what-you-want, bring a bottle of wine to share. Black Cat open mic: free, $2 donation. Lake Eustis Folk: $7 suggested plus a potluck dish. Milk District Salon at 1U: $125 for 6 events (~$21). trad_dance.notes: Contra is $15, free for students, the out-of-work and second-time dancers. Irish sessions, bluegrass jams, the Cassia concert-jam, shape-note singings and the library dulcimer jam are free. Barberville jams cost a $6 park fee. FSFA membership is $20. Claddagh charges no cover for live music.

character_notes.trad_dance: Orlando's trad scene is small, suburban and Sunday-afternoon shaped. Its anchor is one owner-run neighborhood pub, Claddagh Cottage, whose fiddler and banjo-player owners have hosted the Every-Other-Wednesday session for 25 years. Around it run a monthly circuit of Sunday-afternoon Irish sessions in Maitland, Apopka and College Park, a hidden Friday old-time jam in members' homes, and a 35-year-old bluegrass jam held in an Ocoee strip-mall parking lot. Bluegrass's deeper roots are rural and Lake County (Cassia, Kissimmee's Vassar Clements). Contra was rebuilt in 2022 as an explicitly young, gender-neutral, sometimes-techno dance in Winter Park. Shape-note singing re-emerged with an annual all-day singing only in 2024. The retiree square-dance world is real but sits at the edges: in The Villages, Seminole County and the Volusia/Brevard coast rather than in Orlando proper. Theme parks add a professional Celtic layer (Epcot's Off Kilter, Raglan Road) whose alumni turn up at the local pub.

headline_stats.distinct_traditions_active_note: Approximate: 22 heritage traditions judged active or thriving, plus about 12 Layer 1-3 traditions with current recurring events (Irish, old-time, bluegrass, dulcimer, gypsy jazz, contra, modern western square, international, Israeli, shape-note, folk song/songwriter, ukulele). Medium confidence.

costs.notes: Orlando Contra $15; free for students, job-seekers and second-time dancers. Central Florida Folk concerts $15 suggested ($10 members). Timucua shows '$30 or less', about half pay-what-you-want (bring a bottle to share). Black Cat open mic $2 donation; Lake Eustis Folk $7 plus a potluck dish. Irish sessions, bluegrass and old-time jams, shape-note singings and the library dulcimer jam are free; Barberville jams (outside the MSA) $6 park fee. Hiring a touring act for a private house concert: $600-1,500 (one artist's posted rate).

surprises: The session hosts bought the pub. Vicki Gish and Scott Vocca met at Claddagh Cottage's session, ran it from 2001, and bought the pub in 2016. The building was demolished within three months, so they rebuilt 'every detail' at a new address in 2018. The session turned 25 on Sep 9, 2026, and the pub now hosts the six-state South East Tionól and 'Irish C' sessions pitched down a whole step for pipers.
Florida's best-known weekly bluegrass jam happens in a strip-mall parking lot behind a Pizza Hut in Ocoee, every Friday since about 1990. One 86-year-old regular has built 77 mandolins.

Florida cattle drives had fiddlers. Clayton Raulerson (1906-2000) of Narcoossee said every cattle team from Lake Okeechobee to Orlando carried one, because the fiddle 'was the only thing... you could move around'. The metro's only WPA fiddle recording is a cowhunter string band at Caruja Ranch, Kenansville, in 1940, playing 'Shear 'Em' and 'Pastime Annie'.
Kissimmee's Silver Spurs Rodeo began as a square dance on horseback (Quadrille) in 1940. Quadrille teams still practise weekly, and Osceola County schools close for 'Rodeo Day'.
Vassar Clements, Bill Monroe's fiddler and 'Father of Hillbilly Jazz', grew up in Kissimmee, and 'The Kissimmee Kid' was played by Old & In the Way with Jerry Garcia.

Theme parks quietly imported tradition bearers. Epcot's Mariachi Cobre has played the Mexico pavilion since opening day in 1982, Disney recruited a hula troupe in 1971, and the Canada pavilion's Off Kilter played for 17 years. Several of these musicians later won Florida Folk Heritage Awards, and Off Kilter alumni now play the Claddagh session.

Orange County had the second-largest Puerto Rican population of any US county in 2018, behind only the Bronx. The great-granddaughter of bomba patriarch Rafael Cepeda teaches bomba on Tuesday nights in a Kissimmee elementary school, yet no trovador club or weekly cuatro circle turned up.
A 2026 NEA National Heritage Fellow, the conguero Giovanni Hidalgo, lives in Ocoee. The 2006 Fellow Diomedes Matos, master cuatro maker, lives just over the line in Deltona.

Zora Neale Hurston staged an Eatonville folk concert at Rollins College in 1933. Two years later the Lomax trip recorded 104 songs in Eatonville, and in 1939 the WPA recorded a Slovak Lutheran youth choir in Slavia, near Oviedo.

Not one FM station in the metro carries a folk, bluegrass or Celtic show. Arguably the metro's widest-heard folk 'program' is a website: Orlando resident Roger McGuinn's Folk Den, a traditional song every month since 1995.
Orlando Contra calls itself 'Florida's only gender-neutral contra series'. It is designed for 18-30-year-olds, runs some nights to DJ'd techno, and lets second-time dancers in free.
For decades the Orlando folk concert calendar simply stopped every May: 'No Show - See You at the Florida Folk Festival', 175 miles north.
curiosities: Theme parks as heritage employers: how many trad and heritage musicians has Walt Disney World employed over time, and do Anaheim, Las Vegas, Branson or Pigeon Forge show the same pattern of park musicians seeding local scenes?
Bomba classes and jíbaro/trova activity per Puerto Rican resident: why is jíbaro music so thin in Orlando compared with New York, Chicago and Hartford, given a population of about 400,000?

Is Orlando's Sunday-afternoon session circuit (a different pub on the 1st, 3rd and 4th Sundays) typical of car-dependent, retiree-heavy Sun Belt metros (Tampa, Phoenix), compared with the weeknight pub sessions of Boston or Chicago?
Is Orlando the only top-20 metro with no terrestrial folk, bluegrass or Celtic radio show?
Do Orlando's sessions and dances swell with snowbirds? Festivals cluster in Jan-Feb and several groups stop for summer; compare Phoenix and Tampa.
Why did modern western square dancing nearly vanish from Orlando's core while it thrives in The Villages and on the coast? Compare Tampa, Phoenix (Sun City) and Riverside.
Did other Sun Belt cities see Orlando's post-COVID generational reset in contra, from an older potluck dance to a youth-targeted, gender-neutral, partly techno series?

Cattle-country fiddling: do Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, Phoenix or Denver have WPA-era recordings of working cowhands' fiddle bands like Kenansville 1940? Does any living Osceola fiddler carry that repertoire?
How many top-20 metros have an 'invisible' old-time scene living on a private home-jam email list, and how can such scenes be counted fairly?
Is the owner-hosted session (pub owners who are the session leaders) more durable than sessions that depend on a manager's goodwill?
Are state fiddle contests generally rural? Florida's runs 170 miles north at White Springs; which top-20 metros host their state championship?
Is dulcimer and ukulele club participation larger than session participation in retiree-heavy Florida metros?
data_quality_notes:
MERGE NOTES (session coordinator): four parallel research threads (trad_dance, song_listening, heritage, history_festivals) were merged by name; per-row _threads shows the source. Headline per-month totals exclude rows outside the MSA (Brevard, Volusia and Hillsborough sessions, dances and singings are listed but not counted) and rows without a regular frequency (parranda season, trova afternoons). Folk open mics include several low-confidence listings from aggregator sites (Fiddler's Green, Spill, Copper Rocket, Friar Tuck, Serendipity Brews). The Friday old-time home jam (3.5 a month) is low confidence: it runs on a private email list. Orlando has far fewer recurring events than Chicago, so its per-month numbers are more sensitive to single listings. No fiddle contest exists inside the MSA. Per-thread notes follow.

[heritage] Searches ran through DuckDuckGo HTML results plus direct fetches, because the web_search tool was mostly rate-limited. Facebook and Instagram pages could not be opened, so many 2025-26 dates rest on search-result snippets of social posts (marked medium). The NEA fellow search was done by scanning all 502 arts.gov fellow profiles for 'Florida': only Hidalgo (Ocoee, 2026) is inside the MSA; Matos (Deltona) is just outside. Florida Folk Heritage Award bios were scanned for metro place names; 2025's single recipient (Pedro Zepeda) is not local and 2026 recipients were not found. Founding years computed from edition numbers (Highland Games, Greek Fest, Viva Osceola, Pioneer Day, Thundering Spirit, Festival Vallenato, Bajada de la Chinita) are approximate, and sources disagree for the Greek Fest (1962 vs about 1979) and the Highland Games edition count. Not found: Haitian rara, a Filipino rondalla, a Cuban rumba circle, Vietnamese traditional instrumental groups, community klezmer, a standing trova or cuatro society, joropo dance classes, sacred steel congregations in the MSA, and any living Cracker fiddle tradition. Troy Demps's current status (alive, still lining) is unknown; the latest evidence is from 2013. Weekly residencies (Savalou Twoubadou, gaita Fridays) are performances in restaurants rather than open jams. Atlas of Home and festival-aggregator sites were used only for leads, not for counts.

[history_festivals] Several key sources (Florida Memory, the Orange County Regional History Center, tunearch.org, slippery-hill.com) blocked automated fetches. Facts from them come from search-result snippets or secondary pages and are marked medium or low confidence. Web search was heavily rate-limited, so coverage of 1970s-80s Orlando bluegrass clubs, the Orlando Fringe (not investigated), Mount Dora and Sanford festivals (none found beyond Mount Dora's Blueberry Festival) and Seminole/Creek music in the metro is thin. The Library of Congress WPA collection was queried directly through its JSON API: location facets give Seminole Co. (30 items, all Slavia), Osceola Co. (11, all Kenansville) and none for Orange or Lake Co. Hurston's Eatonville songs were recorded in Jacksonville. Founding years inferred from 'Nth annual' counts (Highland Games c.1979, Barberville Jamboree 1977, Lake County Folk Festival 1998) are approximate. Conflicts: Rosie O'Grady's opened in 1974 (Wikipedia, Orlando Signal Apple Annie's article) or 1972 (Orlando Signal Cheyenne article); the official-contest bill was 1989 (FSFA) or 1990 (secondary); Timucua was founded in 2000 (25th anniversary 2025; Orange County) or 1990 (Visit Orlando, probably an error), with 1,000 shows by July 2025 versus '1,400+' cited in Oct 2025; Hoop-Dee-Doo opened June 14 or June 30, 1974 (full-time Sept 5, 1974); the Highland Games 2026 edition is called both the 48th and the 46th. The Kissimmee Bluegrass Festival's end date is unknown. ZORA! attendance figures are secondary. NEA Fellows were checked against arts.gov's Florida filter, which may be incomplete.

[song_listening] Web search was heavily rate-limited during this pass, so many items rest on a single primary source (often an organization's own page or Susan Foster-Trewick's folk open-mic directory, updated Aug 1, 2026). General open mics from that directory are included with low confidence and are not folk-specific. Facebook-only evidence (CFF Song Circle page, Black Cat events) could not be opened; I used aggregator copies of FB events (2025) and organization pages instead. Time conflicts are noted (Black Cat start time). CFF's 'last Sunday' billing conflicts with its listed dates. The Lake Eustis Folk monthly cadence is inferred from two third-Saturday listings. Not found or not verified: any current WPRK/WMFE/WUCF folk show; Gallery at Avalon Island, Snap Space and The Abbey folk programming; Rollins/UCF community folk classes; a historic Central Florida instrument maker; the current status of Lake County Folk Festival, Polasek Folk Fridays and the Orlando FOFF spin-off; Will McLean's specific Orlando residence (sources tie him to the Ocklawaha/Marion County, outside the MSA). Kissimmee/Osceola showed no folk-specific song events. Geocodes are from OSM Nominatim; Timucua's is street-level only.

[trad_dance] Strongest evidence: Claddagh Cottage (live public Google Calendar through 2027), Orlando Contra (site plus CDSS API), the shape-note site (updated 28 Oct 2026) and fasola minutes, Cassia (Bluegrass Today Mar 2026), and the square-dance federation pages (updated Oct 2026). The three Sunday Irish sessions (An Tobar, Stephie's, Castle), the Broken Strings old-time jam and the Friday home jam rest mainly on one source, the FSFA 'Regular Jams' page (updated Feb 2026), plus one EventHound listing for Broken Strings. The pubs' own sites do not mention them, so frequency and start times may drift. The Ocoee jam has strong history (2020, 2023 articles) but no dated 2025-26 news; current status rests on a 2026 jamfinder listing. The Israeli dance and OIFDC listings come from directories updated June 2025. No current Scottish country dance class, English country dance, céilí or set-dance class, morris team, sea-shanty sing, Scandinavian, klezmer or Balkan group was found inside the MSA. A participatory Southern-gospel 'all-day singing' tradition was not found either: searches returned only touring-quartet concerts at Lake County churches. The Villages straddles Lake and Sumter counties; only the La Hacienda (Lake Co.) square dance is counted in-MSA, though Villages clubs (e.g. a SeaBreeze Recreation Center bluegrass jam, Irish American Claddagh Club) are in Sumter and excluded. Facebook groups (Orlando contra, OrlandoFaSoLa, CFBA, Hoedowners) were not readable. Founding years for the Highland Games and FSFA are inferred from edition numbers. The web_search tool was heavily rate-limited, which limited coverage of Kissimmee, St. Cloud, Sanford and Clermont; jams in RV parks and 55+ communities in Lake and Osceola are likely undercounted.
surprises_all_threads: Kissimmee's Silver Spurs Rodeo, which sells out an 8,300-seat arena, began as a square dance on horseback: Osceola ranch kids riding Quadrille after a May 1940 barbecue. Peewee, junior and adult Quadrille teams still practice weekly.

A 2026 NEA National Heritage Fellow lives in Ocoee: conga virtuoso Giovanni Hidalgo (Dizzy Gillespie's United Nations Orchestra, Planet Drum). The 2006 Fellow Diomedes Matos, the 'master's master' of the Puerto Rican cuatro, lives in Deltona, just over the MSA line.

Theme parks quietly imported tradition bearers: Disney recruited a hula troupe for its 1971 opening (Brandt), SeaWorld brought hula master Henry Ohumukini in 1983, Ann Yao came as Epcot's China Pavilion zheng soloist, and Epcot hired Penaflor's Mexican ensemble in 1996. Several later won Florida Folk Heritage Awards.
The great-granddaughter of Don Rafael Cepeda, patriarch of bomba, teaches bomba on Tuesday nights in an elementary-school cafeteria and library in Kissimmee, with drums supplied.
Three months after Hurricane Maria, a plena group 'asalto' at a Kissimmee Walmart drew 2 million+ views; they had done the same the year before.

Orange County had the second-largest Puerto Rican population of any US county in 2018 (209,151, behind only the Bronx), and Osceola had the highest share of any county anywhere outside the island (33.7%).

Clayton Raulerson (1906-2000) said every cattle team driving from Lake Okeechobee to the Orlando area carried a fiddler, the only instrument 'you could move around'. He later built Stradivari-pattern fiddles in Narcoossee and repaired fiddles for Nashville players.

Despite the huge Puerto Rican population, no standing trovador club or weekly cuatro circle turned up; jibaro music shows up in restaurant trova duels and cuatro workshops, while Afro-Puerto Rican bomba has the only dedicated school.
Orlando was the state's hub for African American hymn lining: Deacon Troy Demps trained at least eight apprentices through the state program between 1995 and 2009.
Venezuelan gaita keeps its Maracaibo season in exile: a Friday-night residency runs only from October to January, ending with the Feria de la Chinita.
Orlando's oldest pipe band got its name from a saloon: Church Street Station's Rosie O'Grady's sponsored it from 1980 and had it play Saturday nights.

The metro's only WPA fiddle recording is a cowhunter string band (two 'violins', banjo, guitar) at Caruja Ranch, Kenansville, Osceola County, on July 1, 1940, playing 'Shear 'Em' and 'Pastime Annie'. The same session recorded Black singers James Brown and Rufus Bland, including the jook song 'Uncle Bud' that Hurston also sang from Eatonville tradition.

In 1939 the Library of Congress/WPA recorded a Slovak Lutheran youth choir in Slavia, near Oviedo in Seminole County, singing Slovak folk songs and the Czech and Slovak national anthems: 30 items from a 1911 colony of Cleveland Slovaks.

Florida cattle drives had fiddlers. Clayton Raulerson (1906-2000) of Narcoossee drove cattle from Lake Okeechobee to Orlando, and every cattle team had a fiddle player for the campfire, because the fiddle 'was the only thing back then we had that you could move around.'

A Church Street bar was nationally televised country music: TNN filmed a weekly concert series at the Cheyenne Saloon for 8 seasons (1984-92), with Garth Brooks, Alan Jackson and Travis Tritt before they were famous. In 1985 Church Street drew 1.7 million visitors, behind only Disney, SeaWorld and Busch Gardens in Florida.

Winter Park's 1960s Carrera Room, a coffeehouse inside a breakfast diner, hosted Gram Parsons, 17-year-old future Eagle Bernie Leadon, Fred Neil and Don Reno, and paid 14-year-old Jeanie Fitchen $8 a night to host the open mic.
Vassar Clements, 'The Kissimmee Kid', has a fiddle tune named for his Osceola County hometown, and it was played by Old & In the Way with Jerry Garcia.

Epcot has been one of the metro's longest-lasting heritage-music employers: Mariachi Cobre has played the Mexico pavilion since opening day in 1982, taiko ran from 1983 until COVID ended it on March 15, 2020, and the bagpipe-led Off Kilter played the Canada pavilion for 17 years. Its piper started out at Rosie O'Grady's on Church Street.

In 1933 Zora Neale Hurston staged an Eatonville folk concert ('From Sun to Sun: A Day in a Railroad Camp') at Rollins College, with an all-Black cast before a white-only audience, two years before Lomax recorded 104 songs in Eatonville.

Osceola County public schools close for 'Rodeo Day' (Silver Spurs Rodeo, since 1944) instead of Presidents' Day: cracker cattle culture is still on the school calendar in the county of Disney's southern gates.

Eatonville is routinely billed as America's oldest incorporated Black town, but Brooklyn, Illinois (1873) is older, and Sanford had its own Black town, Goldsboro (incorporated 1891), until Sanford annexed it in 1911.

Orlando's 2026 NEA National Heritage Fellow is a world-famous conguero: Giovanni Hidalgo (Dizzy Gillespie, Paul Simon, Mickey Hart's Planet Drum) lives in Ocoee, and the master cuatro maker Diomedes Matos (2006 Fellow) is just over the county line in Deltona.

Apple Annie's folk-bluegrass house band Mother's Choice had a Disney monorail parody of 'Charlie on the M.T.A.' (Charlie, lacking a ticket, rides forever round the Magic Kingdom), now preserved as an MP3 on Orlando Memory.

Byrds founder Roger McGuinn, described by the Orlando Sentinel as an 'Orlando resident', has recorded and posted a traditional folk song online every month since 1995 (his 'Folk Den'). It was still going on Oct 1, 2026 with 'Little Brown Jug'. Arguably the metro's most widely heard folk 'program' is a website, not a radio show.
Gamble Rogers, Florida's best-loved folk troubadour, was born in Winter Park, son of the architect whose 1930s Casa Feliz now hosts 'Music at the Casa' and Florida poetry-and-song nights.
Orlando's folk club holds its monthly concerts in a library designed by Sir David Adjaye. The old Winter Park library building is now the Blue Bamboo listening room (reopened June 2025).

Timucua, the metro's top listening room, is a family home built around a 90-seat concert hall by Cirque du Soleil's La Nouba music director, with an active acoustic system. Guests bring a bottle of wine to share; about half the shows are pay-what-you-want. In Jan 2026 its chamber-music festival booked Cape Breton fiddle-and-piano sisters Cassie and Maggie MacDonald.
The Black Cat Cafe open mic was named for the Friday the 13th in May 1994 when it started in a Unitarian church hall. It has run monthly for over 30 years and still asks only a $2 donation.
For decades the Orlando folk concert calendar simply stopped every May: 'No Show - See You at the Florida Folk Festival', 175 miles north in White Springs.
Orlando's leading dulcimer player, Bing Futch, won 'Best Guitarist' at the 2016 International Blues Challenge without playing a guitar: he played mountain dulcimer.
Not one FM station in the Orlando metro carried a folk, bluegrass or Celtic show in Oct 2026. WPRK's roughly 80 shows include polka/disco, Bollywood and reggae, but no folk.
The dulcimer club OASIS meets in a guitar shop in Eatonville, Zora Neale Hurston's hometown.
Central Florida Folk's membership list is published online with names and expiry dates: 13 current members for a metro of nearly 3 million, yet it books 9-10 touring and local acts a year.
The Leu Gardens folk series skipped every March for the gardens' Flower Show and held a 'No Guitars Allowed' concert most Septembers (hammered dulcimer, piano, storytelling).

The session hosts bought the pub. Vicki Gish and Scott Vocca met at Claddagh Cottage's session, ran it from 2001, bought the pub in 2016, lost the building to demolition less than three months later, and painstakingly rebuilt 'every detail' of the pub at a new address in 2018. The session's 25th anniversary was 9 Sep 2026.

Florida's best-known weekly bluegrass jam happens in a strip-mall parking lot behind a Pizza Hut in Ocoee, on the site of an old Piggly Wiggly. It has run every Friday since about 1990, and an 86-year-old regular has built 77 mandolins.
Vassar Clements, the 'Father of Hillbilly Jazz' and Bill Monroe's fiddler from 1949 to 1956, grew up in Kissimmee. His cousins were regulars at the Cassia jams in rural Lake County.

Despite the retiree reputation, modern western square dancing barely exists in Orlando proper. The Federation lists only Casselberry, Oviedo and Geneva clubs in the core, while The Villages, Ocala and the coast have the rest, and one caller (Rod Barngrover) works clubs from Casselberry to Ocala to Ormond Beach.

Orlando Contra markets itself as 'Florida's only gender-neutral contra series', designs its dances for 18-30-year-olds, runs some nights to DJ'd techno, and lets students, job-seekers and anyone at 'your second contra ever' in free.
Orlando hosted the 2025 Comhaltas North American Convention at a SeaWorld-area hotel, even though no Comhaltas branch exists in Central Florida.

A neighborhood pub is the Southeast's uilleann-pipe hub. Claddagh Cottage hosts the six-state South East Tionól, International Uilleann Piping Day ('Try the Pipes!') and occasional 'Irish C sessions' played a whole step down.

Theme-park Celtic musicians cycle into the local scene: ex-Off Kilter (Epcot, 1997-2014) members Billy Varnes and fiddler Colin Farrell, plus Disney-band veteran and former state fiddle champion Jason Thomas, all play Claddagh Cottage.

At the 2024 Orlando all-day Sacred Harp singing, the famed Alabama singer David Ivey recalled singing in Central Florida in the 1960s. The revived singing's Sunday leg now goes to a traditional Primitive Baptist church near Tampa that sings from the Cooper Book.

The RSCDS 'Orlando Branch' is the umbrella for ten Scottish country dance groups from Pensacola to Broward, yet no current Orlando class could be verified. The nearest verified weekly classes are on the Space Coast.
There is a gypsy-jazz jam in an Irish pub. Claddagh added a monthly Django-style jam in 2025.
Mount Dora's dulcimer society holds its monthly jam in the public library, which lends ukuleles to anyone who wants to join.
